title: Weave module manifest
description: Declared by every module: authored as module.manifest.json in the module's source directory, embedded in the module binary for handshake cross-checking, and published as a signed sidecar whose distribution subset is carried in the channel manifest.

protocol.description: The single protocol integer this module speaks.

zone.description: Build zone: A = static CGO_ENABLED=0, B = UI-runtime-coupled pure Go, C = cgo/entitled.

privilege.description: Privilege the supervisor grants at spawn. Not every module is root. system: core's own identity. service: the unprivileged service account (a restricted token on Windows). user: the console user — only with session per-user-console, which in turn requires it.

session.description: Where the process lives. system: core's child in core's own session. per-user-console: core's child inside the session of the user at the physical console (the macOS GUI session, the Linux logind seat0 session, the Windows active console session), running as that user; started when someone logs in, stopped when they leave, moved when the console changes hands. per-user-all is reserved: core refuses it.

capabilities.description: Capability names the module requires; core gates launch on these.

address.description: Name the module answers to on the hypervisor channel when it differs from id, e.g. weave.exec shared by the per-OS builds of one capability. Core refuses two installed modules with the same address. Defaults to id.

subscribes.description: Event-bus topic patterns this module may subscribe to (exact or "<prefix>.*"). Core enforces this allow-list at Subscribe; empty means the module subscribes to nothing.

authenticode_thumbprint.description: SHA-1 thumbprint of the Authenticode signing certificate, 40 hex digits in either case. Sufficient on its own, and preferred over authenticode_subject; given both, both must match.

signing.description: Identity core pins when verifying the binary before exec.

artifacts.description: Stamped by CI at publish; absent in the authored source file.
